full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case as stated in the petition are that the House No. 1/15, Block-D, Razia Sultana Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka, measuring an area of 144 square yards originally belonged to the then Government of East Pakistan and that the Government leased out the aforesaid property to Syed Md Yunus by a registered deed of lease being No. 2067 dated 2-2-1960; that after taking delivery of possession of the aforesaid property the original allottee Syed Md Yunus built a two-storied building on the leasehold land and had been living therein with his family members and that said Syed Md Yunus being in need of urgent cash money sold out the aforesaid building to Md Abdul Quayum by a registered deed being No. 881 dated 3-2-1969 and delivered physical possession of the building in question to said Abdul Quayum and that thereafter, Abdul Quayum while was in ownership and possession of the property he again sold out the same to one Habiba Banu wife of Abdul Ash by a registered deed being No. 3998 dated 30-4-1970 and handed over the physical possession of the house to her on the same day on 30-4-1970; that Habiba Banu, while was in ownership and possession of the aforesaid house she being in need of money sold out the same to the petitioners at a consideration of Taka 40,000 (Taka forty thousand) vide four registered sale deeds being Nos. 2498, 2499, 2500 and 2501 dated 9-12-1972 and handed over the physical possession of the case property along with all original documents of the building in question; that thereafter, aforesaid Habiba Banu left the property and shifted her family to a rented house situated at 22 Bangshal Road, under PS Kotwali, District-Dhaka. The petitioners also stated that Abdul Ash, the husband of Habiba Banu, was a Bangladesh national and a resident of village Ashugonj, under PS and District Brahmanbaria, that the petitioners mutated their names in the office of the City Corporation and got electricity, gas and WASA connection in the case property in their own names and Khatians in respect of the case property has been opened in their names and they have been paying taxes and other bills regularly; that while the petitioners were in ownership and possession of the case property the State Officer under the Ministry of Public Works entered into a lease agreement on 10-4-1974 with Abdul Halim, father of the petitioner, in respect of the case property for the residential accommodation of a Government officer and that after hiring the property the government allotted the same to one Mr Md Arifur Rahman, Administrative Officer, Ministry of Planning, Government of Bangladesh on 30-5-1974 for a period of leone) year and that the said agreement was renewed from time to time upto 1987 and paid rent regularly to the petitioners; that after the death of their father, aforesaid Abdul Halirn, petitioner's mother Rahima Khatun accepted the rent from the Government on behalf of the petitioners. The petitioners filed an application to the Assistant Commissioner of Housing and Settlement, Ministry of Public Works, Segunbagicha, Dhaka on 23-1-1984 and 12-4-1984 for mutating their names in place of the previous owner. On receipt of the applications the Assistant Commissioners held an inquiry through their local Administrative Officer who after holding inquiry submitted a report on 25-4-1985 stating that the petitioners are in possession of the case property by purchase from Habiba Banu. The petitioners further stated that they are in exclusive ownership and possession of the case property by purchase from lawful owner but the Government has published a Gazette on 23-9-1986 enlisting the abandoned building and in the said list the house of the petitioners has been included in the kha list of the abandoned building. The petitioners thereafter filed an application before the Court of Settlement under section 7 of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 for the exclusion of the property from the Kha list which was registered as Settlement case No. 172 of 1995. The Court of Settlement after hearing by judgment and order dated 28-5-2000 rejected the case and thereby refused to exclude the case property from the abandoned list. Being aggrieved thereby the petitioners moved this court and obtained the present Rule.
